Indikator 9b measures the 30-day mortality rate among patients with a Charlson Score of 1 or 2 across various regional and local hospital units in Denmark [^src1]. The data highlights significant variation in mortality proportions, ranging from 20.0% to 31.3% across the included facilities [^src1]. 

The lowest mortality rates are observed at [[esbjerg-sygehus-grindsted-sygehus|Esbjerg Sygehus Grindsted Sygehus]] and [[sygehus-lillebaelt|Sygehus Lillebælt]], both recording a 20.0% mortality rate [^src1]. Conversely, the highest mortality rate is found at [[regionshospital-nordjylland|Regionshospital Nordjylland]], where 31.3% of the included patients died within 30 days [^src1]. Other units with notably high mortality rates include [[regionshospitalet-goedstrup|Regionshospitalet Gødstrup]] at 29.7% and the overall [[nordjylland-region-i-alt|Nordjylland Region i alt]] at 27.1% [^src1]. 

Because the dataset consists of a single cross-sectional snapshot, no longitudinal trends or improvements over time can be established [^src1]. Furthermore, no specific clinical targets or thresholds are defined in the provided data to evaluate whether units met or missed standard performance goals [^src1]. 

When examining outliers and statistical stability, it is important to note that some units, particularly [[regionshospital-nordjylland|Regionshospital Nordjylland]] and [[sygehus-lillebaelt|Sygehus Lillebælt]], have relatively small patient cohorts of 16 and 20 patients, respectively [^src1]. This results in wide 95% confidence intervals that overlap heavily with the rates of other hospitals [^src1]. In contrast, larger cohorts such as [[midtjylland-region-i-alt|Midtjylland Region i alt]] with 152 patients and [[odense-universitetshospital-svendborg|Odense Universitetshospital - Svendborg]] with 70 patients provide much narrower confidence intervals and more statistically stable estimates [^src1].
